# Skill: c4-modeling

# C4 Modeling

You are making the modeling decisions for a C4 architecture model — which
abstraction level each element belongs to, what a container is (and what
one is not), how to model external and third-party systems, and how to
name elements and label relationships. How to write the DSL text is the
`structurizr-dsl-authoring` skill's task, and the parse/validate/inspect
loop is the `structurizr-validate-loop` skill's task.

## The decisions

The decisions a model gets wrong most often, in the order the questions
come up:

1. **Pick the abstraction level first.** Person (a user or role), Software
   System (Level 1), Container (Level 2), Component (Level 3), Code
   (Level 4) — each level has a precise meaning; do not conflate them.
2. **A container is a runtime boundary** — a separately running process
   or a data store (a web app, a service, a database, a queue). A
   library, a JAR, a module, or a package is NOT a container: code that
   runs inside another element's process is not its own element. A C4
   container is not a Docker container. When several elements share or
   embed a library, the library is STILL no element — no container, no
   component, and no "embeds" relationship to it; name the library in
   the sharing elements' descriptions instead.
3. **External and third-party systems are top-level, tagged
   `External`.** Something you do not own or operate is a top-level
   `softwareSystem` (or `element`) with the `External` tag — never a
   container inside your system. In this DSL version there is no
   `externalSystem` keyword.
4. **Name and describe every element.** A 1–2 sentence description of its
   responsibility; containers and components carry a technology label.
5. **Label every relationship with its intent and a technology.**
   Unidirectional; "sends notification emails to", never a vague "uses",
   "connects to" or "interacts with"; EVERY relationship names a protocol
   or technology — including person→container relationships (e.g.
   "HTTPS/JSON"); a relationship without a technology is incomplete.
6. **Split containers on runtime boundaries** (independent deployment,
   scaling, technology, availability) — not on code modules. Add
   components only when a container's internal structure is
   architecturally significant.

The full rules — the levels, the notation, the workflow, and the common
mistakes — live in `references/levels-and-notation.md` and
`references/modeling-decisions.md`. Read the file that matches the
decision you are making.

Before you finish, check the workspace text with the structurizr MCP
`validate` tool and fix every error it reports. Keep re-running it on the
fixed text until it answers `OK` — do not finish while `validate` is
still reporting errors, and make sure the file on disk is the exact text
you last validated. A model whose workspace does not validate is not
done. Your host prefixes the MCP tool names (for example
`structurizr_validate`; the in-harness server name is `structurizr`), so
call whichever prefixed variant your host exposes. The full
parse/validate/inspect loop with finding triage is the
`structurizr-validate-loop` skill's task — this skill decides what to
model; that skill proves the text is right.

## The MCP limits

The Structurizr MCP tools have hard limits; keep the workspace within
them:

- **DSL text only, single file.** The tools work on the workspace's DSL
  text given as one input; there is no multi-file workspace. Inline

You are writing or repairing Structurizr DSL — the text format for C4

The rules whose violations surface as parse errors, missing model facts,

with the exact error strings; the short list:

1. **Declare elements before the relationships that use them.** The DSL
   is parsed top to bottom, so a forward reference fails with
   `The destination element "x" does not exist` — the same error as a
   typo. Check the identifier first, then the order.
2. **Quote every value that contains spaces** — names, descriptions,
   technologies, custom-element metadata. Quotes are optional only for a
   single token; an unquoted phrase with more tokens than the statement
   has left over fails with `Too many tokens, expected: ...`. To skip an
   optional property you want to leave empty, use `""`.
3. **Braces:** the opening `{` sits on the same line as the statement;
   the closing `}` sits on a line of its own.
4. **Identifiers are flat and unique** across the whole workspace by
   default (characters `a-zA-Z_0-9`); a second declaration of the same
   identifier fails with `The identifier "x" is already in use`. Rename

   description is the relationship's identity — two relationships with
   the same description are a duplicate.

   string is its metadata).

   spaces).

# Skill: structurizr-validate-loop

# Structurizr Validate Loop

You are checking Structurizr DSL with the Structurizr MCP server. Your
host prefixes the MCP tool names (for example `structurizr_validate`;
the in-harness server name is `structurizr`), so refer to the tools by
their own names — the `parse`, `validate`, and `inspect` tools of the
Structurizr MCP server — and call whichever prefixed variant your host
exposes.

## The mandatory loop

Every DSL result runs through this loop before it is returned:

1. **Parse.** Run the `parse` tool on the DSL text. Fix every error it
   reports and parse again.
2. **Validate until OK.** Run the `validate` tool. If it reports
   errors, fix them and re-run. Keep going until `validate` answers
   `OK` — do not move on, and do not report the model as done, before
   it does.
3. **Inspect.** Run the `inspect` tool on the validated text.
4. **Triage EVERY finding** into exactly one of the three labels:
    - **fix** — correct the DSL. Any edit after the final validate
      requires re-validating, so the fixed text re-enters the loop at
      step 2.
    - **expected under the MCP limits** — the finding is caused by a
      limit of the MCP (below), not by the model. Do not chase it.
    - **reported in the final answer** — a genuine recommendation that
      is not fixed now; state it in the final answer.

    A finding that cannot be cleared under the MCP never blocks the
    result.
5. **Return the exact text that last got `OK` from `validate`.** Never
    return text that was never validated to `OK`, and never return text
    that changed after the final validate: if anything is edited after
    the final validate, re-run `validate` (and `inspect` on the new
    text) before returning.

A DSL result that was only parsed, and not validated to `OK`, is NOT a
pass — a parsed-only or reported-only result is not a pass. This is the
same rule as the repo's own PlantUML validation chain (DEC
7a626b12-b189-4561-a51d-ffb2e9e193b4): a structure-only check is not a
pass.

## How to call the tools

Your host may expose the MCP only through Code Mode: `execute` blocks
that call `tools.<server>.<tool>({ ... })` (discover the server name
first with `tools.opencode.list_mcp_resources()`; in the harness it is
`structurizr`). Four rules keep the loop verifiable:

1. **One MCP call per block, with the raw answer.** Never bundle
   `parse` + `validate` + `inspect` in one block (no `Promise.all`/
   `allSettled`), and never wrap even a single answer: the block
   `return`s the tool's own answer. For a clean `validate` that is
   exactly the two letters `OK`, so write
   `return await tools.structurizr.validate({ dsl: ... });` — not
   `return { validate: result }`. A bundled or wrapped answer hides
   the `OK` and the loop is not done.
2. **No filesystem in Code Mode.** The sandbox has no `fs`, no
   `require`, no `import('node:fs')` and no network: every call takes
   the workspace text inline.
3. **The final `validate` inlines the exact file text as a plain
   literal** — not a variable, not a shorthand:

   ```javascript
   return await tools.structurizr.validate({
     dsl: `workspace "Bookshop" "A simple online bookshop" {
         model { ... }
     }
   `
   });
   ```

   The backtick literal may span lines; it must contain no backslashes
   and no `${` (C4 models do not). Treat `workspace.dsl` as the single
   source of truth: after every edit, the next call inlines the
   file's new text. The `workspace.dsl` on disk must be
   byte-identical to the final literal — same characters, same
   trailing newline: write the file first, then inline exactly what
   the file holds (re-read it right before the final call when in
   doubt). The block answers the two letters `OK` for that exact text
   and only that text; if the file changes afterwards, the loop runs
   again. Never end the task with text that only existed inside a
   code block: the file on disk is the result.
4. **Fix the named error, not a guess.** Parse/validate messages name
   the line and the problem — change exactly that and re-run. Do not
   build experiment harnesses to isolate what the message already said.

## What the two tools answer

`validate` answers "will this parse into a workspace?" — it is
blocking, and its `OK` is the only green light this skill has.
`inspect` answers "does this follow C4 and Structurizr
recommendations?" — its findings are recommendations, never a failed
validate. See `references/validate-vs-inspect.md` for the side-by-side
table and the common findings with their triage.

## Triage and the final answer

Triage every finding of the last `inspect` with one of the three
labels, and end with an answer in this shape — quoting each finding's
exact text:

    Validation: `validate` answered OK on the exact text now in workspace.dsl.
    Findings (triaged):
    - fix: "<the finding's exact text>" — what you changed
    - expected: "<the finding's exact text>" — the MCP refuses `!docs`/`!adrs`
    - reported: "<the finding's exact text>"
    MCP limits: <any limit that shaped the result; name `!include`/`!docs` when relevant>

Only the missing-documentation and missing-decisions findings are
**expected** (the MCP refuses `!docs`/`!adrs` — do not add them).
Everything you fixed is **fix**; everything you left is **reported**.

their own names — the `parse`, `validate`, and `inspect` tools of the
Structurizr MCP server — and call whichever prefixed variant your host
exposes.

## The mandatory loop

Every DSL result runs through this loop before it is returned:

1. **Parse.** Run the `parse` tool on the DSL text. Fix every error it
   reports and parse again.
2. **Validate until OK.** Run the `validate` tool. If it reports
   errors, fix them and re-run. Keep going until `validate` answers
   `OK` — do not move on, and do not report the model as done, before
   it does.
3. **Inspect.** Run the `inspect` tool on the validated text.
4. **Triage EVERY finding** into exactly one of the three labels:
    - **fix** — correct the DSL. Any edit after the final validate
      requires re-validating, so the fixed text re-enters the loop at
      step 2.
    - **expected under the MCP limits** — the finding is caused by a
      limit of the MCP (below), not by the model. Do not chase it.
    - **reported in the final answer** — a genuine recommendation that
      is not fixed now; state it in the final answer.

    A finding that cannot be cleared under the MCP never blocks the
    result.
5. **Return the exact text that last got `OK` from `validate`.** Never
    return text that was never validated to `OK`, and never return text
    that changed after the final validate: if anything is edited after
    the final validate, re-run `validate` (and `inspect` on the new
    text) before returning.

A DSL result that was only parsed, and not validated to `OK`, is NOT a
pass — a parsed-only or reported-only result is not a pass. This is the
same rule as the repo's own PlantUML validation chain (DEC
7a626b12-b189-4561-a51d-ffb2e9e193b4): a structure-only check is not a
pass.

## How to call the tools

Your host may expose the MCP only through Code Mode: `execute` blocks
that call `tools.<server>.<tool>({ ... })` (discover the server name
first with `tools.opencode.list_mcp_resources()`; in the harness it is
`structurizr`). Four rules keep the loop verifiable:

1. **One MCP call per block, with the raw answer.** Never bundle
   `parse` + `validate` + `inspect` in one block (no `Promise.all`/
   `allSettled`), and never wrap even a single answer: the block
   `return`s the tool's own answer. For a clean `validate` that is
   exactly the two letters `OK`, so write
   `return await tools.structurizr.validate({ dsl: ... });` — not
   `return { validate: result }`. A bundled or wrapped answer hides
   the `OK` and the loop is not done.
2. **No filesystem in Code Mode.** The sandbox has no `fs`, no
   `require`, no `import('node:fs')` and no network: every call takes
   the workspace text inline.
3. **The final `validate` inlines the exact file text as a plain
   literal** — not a variable, not a shorthand:

   ```javascript
   return await tools.structurizr.validate({
     dsl: `workspace "Bookshop" "A simple online bookshop" {
         model { ... }
     }
   `
   });
   ```

   The backtick literal may span lines; it must contain no backslashes
   and no `${` (C4 models do not). Treat `workspace.dsl` as the single
   source of truth: after every edit, the next call inlines the
   file's new text. The `workspace.dsl` on disk must be
   byte-identical to the final literal — same characters, same
   trailing newline: write the file first, then inline exactly what
   the file holds (re-read it right before the final call when in
   doubt). The block answers the two letters `OK` for that exact text
   and only that text; if the file changes afterwards, the loop runs
   again. Never end the task with text that only existed inside a
   code block: the file on disk is the result.
4. **Fix the named error, not a guess.** Parse/validate messages name
   the line and the problem — change exactly that and re-run. Do not
   build experiment harnesses to isolate what the message already said.

## What the two tools answer

`validate` answers "will this parse into a workspace?" — it is
blocking, and its `OK` is the only green light this skill has.
`inspect` answers "does this follow C4 and Structurizr
recommendations?" — its findings are recommendations, never a failed
validate. See `references/validate-vs-inspect.md` for the side-by-side
table and the common findings with their triage.

## Triage and the final answer

Triage every finding of the last `inspect` with one of the three
labels, and end with an answer in this shape — quoting each finding's
exact text:

    Validation: `validate` answered OK on the exact text now in workspace.dsl.
    Findings (triaged):
    - fix: "<the finding's exact text>" — what you changed
    - expected: "<the finding's exact text>" — the MCP refuses `!docs`/`!adrs`
    - reported: "<the finding's exact text>"
    MCP limits: <any limit that shaped the result; name `!include`/`!docs` when relevant>

Only the missing-documentation and missing-decisions findings are
**expected** (the MCP refuses `!docs`/`!adrs` — do not add them).
Everything you fixed is **fix**; everything you left is **reported**.

## The MCP limits

The Structurizr MCP tools have hard limits; state them in the final
answer whenever they affect the result:

- **DSL text only, single file.** The tools work on the workspace's
  DSL text given as one input; there is no multi-file workspace.
- **`!include`, `!docs`, and `!adrs` are refused.** They answer, for
  example, `!include <file> is not permitted (feature
  structurizr.feature.dsl.filesystem is not enabled)` or `!docs is not
  permitted (feature ... documentation is not enabled)`. At most one
  attempt: if the multi-file workspace the task asks for gets that
  refusal, stop trying multi-file shapes and fall back to a single
  file — inline everything into `workspace.dsl` (no `!include`,
  `!docs`, or `!adrs` in the final text), run the loop on that file,
  and keep any `docs/` folder on disk for the CLI workflow; the final
  `workspace.dsl` simply does not reference it. Never use a `!theme`
  with a URL (offline validation cannot fetch it). In the final answer,
  name `!include` and `!docs` and say why the single file deviates.
- **No image rendering.** The MCP cannot produce image files (PNG/SVG).
  Its export tools emit diagram source only — PlantUML, C4-PlantUML,
  or Mermaid text. If images are requested, say so.

## When the MCP is absent

If the Structurizr MCP tools are not available in the host, validation
is not possible. State that in the final answer and never describe a
DSL result as validated — a result the tools could not check is
unvalidated, no matter how well it looks.

## Gotchas that surface in the loop

`references/dsl-gotchas.md` collects the DSL rules whose violations the
loop most often meets: declaration order (elements before the
relationships that use them), quoting, a description and a technology
on every relationship, flat identifiers, and explicit view keys.

2: 
3: ## When to Split a Container
4: 
5: Split when:
6: 
7: - Parts deploy independently
8: - Parts scale independently
9: - Parts use different technology stacks
10: - Parts have different availability requirements
11: 
12: Do NOT split when:
13: 
14: - It's just different modules in the same process
15: - You want to show internal structure (use components instead)
16: 
17: ## When to Add Components
18: 
19: Add components when:
20: 
21: - The container's internal structure is architecturally significant
22: - You need to show how responsibilities are distributed
23: - There are important interfaces between internal parts
24: 
25: Skip components when:
26: 
27: - The container is simple enough to understand from its description
28: - Components would just mirror the folder structure
29: - The diagram would have too many elements to be useful
30: 
31: ## When to Model External Systems
32: 
33: Model as an external software system when:
34: 
35: - You don't own or control it
36: - It's operated by a different team/organization
37: - You interact with it through a defined API/protocol
38: 
39: Model as a container within your system when:
40: 
41: - You deploy and manage it (even if it's third-party software like
42:   PostgreSQL)
43: - It's part of your system's infrastructure
44: 
45: In this DSL version there is no `externalSystem` keyword: an external
46: system is a **top-level** `softwareSystem` (or `element`) carrying the
47: `External` tag, outside the owned system:
48: 
49: ```
50: emailProvider = softwareSystem "Email Delivery Service" "Delivers notification emails on behalf of the platform." "External"
51: ```
52: 
53: The owned system's containers point at it with their relationships
54: (`dispatch -> emailProvider "sends notification emails to" "REST/JSON"`).
55: Because the keyword does not exist, the export JSON's `externalSystems`
56: section is never populated by this DSL — the fact to look for is the
57: `External` tag on a top-level element, and a third-party service that
58: ended up as a container inside the owned system is a modeling mistake.
59: 
60: ## Common Mistakes
61: 
62: 1. **Confusing containers with Docker containers** — C4 containers are
63:    runtime boundaries
64: 2. **Treating libraries as containers** — JARs, packages, modules are
65:    code-level, not containers. When several elements share or embed a
66:    library, the library is still no element: no container, no component,
67:    no "embeds" relationship — name it in the sharing elements'
68:    descriptions instead
69: 3. **Vague relationship labels** — "Uses" says nothing; describe the
70:    intent
71: 4. **Missing technology on inter-container relationships** — always
72:    specify protocol
73: 5. **Too many components** — only model architecturally significant
74:    groupings
75: 6. **Mixing abstraction levels** — don't show components and external
76:    systems at the same level in a container diagram
77: 7. **Creating component/code diagrams that won't be maintained** — if
78:    it'll go stale, don't create it
79: 8. **Missing titles or legends** — every diagram needs both
80: 9. **Modeling organizational structure** — C4 models software, not teams

86: | System Context | Slow | Low — create and maintain |

88: | Component | Fast during development | Medium — create only if valuable |

1: # Structurizr DSL syntax
2: 
3: The syntax reference for writing `workspace.dsl` text. Adapted from the
4: `structurizr-dsl` skill of `jrjsmrtn/c4-skills` (MIT, see `NOTICE.md`)
5: with details from the Structurizr documentation
6: (`structurizr/structurizr.github.io`, MIT); see `source-map.md` for the
7: passage-by-passage mapping.
8: 
9: ## Syntax fundamentals
10: 
11: - Lines are processed **sequentially** — no forward references
12: - Keywords are **case-insensitive** (`softwareSystem` = `softwaresystem`)
13: - Double quotes are optional for single-word values without spaces
14: - Opening `{` must be on the **same line** as the statement
15: - Closing `}` must be on its **own line**
16: - Opening/closing braces are only required when adding child content
17: - Use `""` as a placeholder for an earlier optional property that you
18:   want to skip (for example `person "Name" "" "Tag"` — no description,
19:   but a tag)
20: - Tags are comma separated (`"Tag 1,Tag 2,Tag 3"`)
21: - Comments: `//` or `#` (single-line), `/* ... */` (multi-line)
22: - Line continuation: `\` as the last character on the line
23: - Identifier characters: `a-zA-Z_0-9`
24: 
25: ### Constants and Variables
26: 
27: ```dsl
28: !const SYSTEM_NAME "My System"        # immutable
29: !var VERSION "1.0"                    # redefinable
30: # Reference: ${SYSTEM_NAME}, ${VERSION}
31: ```
32: 
33: Constant and variable names may only contain `a-zA-Z0-9-_.`. String
34: substitution runs on any token written as `${NAME}`, where `NAME` is a
35: constant, a variable, or an environment variable; a name that cannot be
36: found is left unsubstituted.
37: 
38: ## Workspace structure
39: 
40: ```dsl
41: workspace [name] [description] {
42:     !identifiers hierarchical          # recommended for non-trivial models
43:     !impliedRelationships true         # default: auto-creates parent relationships
44: 
45:     model {
46:         # people, systems, relationships
47:     }
48: 
49:     views {
50:         # diagram definitions, styles, themes
51:     }
52: 
53:     configuration {
54:         # scope, visibility, users
55:     }
56: }
57: ```

2: 
3: The view, style, theme and configuration syntax of `workspace.dsl`.
4: Adapted from the `structurizr-dsl` skill of `jrjsmrtn/c4-skills` (MIT,

8: ## Views
9: 
10: Every view should carry an **explicit key** (characters `a-zA-Z0-9_-`,
11: no spaces) — a view without a key gets an auto-generated one that is not
12: guaranteed to be stable over time, and you will likely lose manual
13: layout information.
14: 
15: ### System Landscape
16: 
17: ```dsl
18: systemLandscape [key] [description] {
19:     include *
20:     autoLayout [tb|bt|lr|rl] [rankSep] [nodeSep]
21:     title "Title"
22:     description "..."
23: }
24: ```
25: 
26: ### System Context
27: 
28: ```dsl
29: systemContext <systemId> [key] [description] {
30:     include *
31:     autoLayout
32:     title "System Context for X"
33: }
34: ```
35: 
36: ### Container View
37: 
38: ```dsl
39: container <systemId> [key] [description] {
40:     include *
41:     autoLayout
42:     title "Containers for X"
43: }
44: ```
45: 
46: ### Component View
47: 
48: ```dsl
49: component <containerId> [key] [description] {
50:     include *
51:     autoLayout
52:     title "Components of X"
53: }
54: ```
55: 
56: ### Dynamic View
57: 
58: ```dsl
59: dynamic <scope> [key] [description] {
60:     # scope: * (people/systems), systemId (+ containers), containerId (+ components)
61:     <source> -> <destination> [description] [technology]
62:     <source> -> <destination> [description] [technology]
63:     autoLayout
64:     title "Feature Y Flow"
65: }
66: ```
67: 
68: Interactions are automatically numbered in order. To set explicit
69: ordering:
70: 
71: ```dsl
72: dynamic <scope> [key] [description] {
73:     1: user -> system.api "submits order" "HTTPS"
74:     2: system.api -> system.db "persists order" "SQL"
75:     3: system.api -> system.queue "publishes event" "AMQP"
76: }
77: ```
78: 
79: ### Deployment View
80: 
81: ```dsl
82: deployment <systemId|*> <environment> [key] [description] {
83:     include *
84:     autoLayout
85:     title "Production Deployment"
86: }
87: ```
88: 
89: ### Filtered View
90: 
91: ```dsl
92: filtered <baseViewKey> <include|exclude> <tags> [key] [description]
93: ```
94: 
95: Creates a view on top of another, filtering elements by tags. The base
96: view is hidden when a filtered view exists.
97: 
98: ### AutoLayout
99: 
100: ```dsl
101: autoLayout [direction] [rankSeparation] [nodeSeparation]
102: # direction: tb (default), bt, lr, rl
103: # default separations: 300px each
104: ```
105: 
106: ### Include/Exclude with Expressions
107: 
108: Element expressions:
109: 
110: ```dsl
111: include element.type==Container
112: include element.tag==Database
113: include element.tag!=External
114: include element.parent==<id>
115: include element.technology==PostgreSQL
116: include ->system.api->                 # elements connected to system.api (both directions)
117: include ->system.api                   # elements that depend on system.api (afferent)
118: include system.api->                   # elements system.api depends on (efferent)
119: ```
120: 
121: Combine with `&&` (AND) and `||` (OR):
122: 
123: ```dsl
124: include element.type==Container && element.tag!=External
125: ```
126: 
127: Relationship expressions:
128: 
129: ```dsl
130: include * -> *                         # all relationships between included elements
131: include user -> *                      # all relationships from user
132: include * -> system.db                 # all relationships to database
133: include relationship.tag==Async
134: include relationship==system.api->system.db
135: ```
136: 
137: The reluctant wildcard includes everything `*` does, minus orphaned
138: elements (elements with no relationships in the view):
139: 
140: ```dsl
141: include *?
142: ```
143: 
144: `exclude` takes the same expressions.

146: ## Styles
147: 
148: ### Element Styles
149: 
150: ```dsl
151: styles {
152:     element <tag> {
153:         shape <shape>                  # see shapes below
154:         icon <file|url>
155:         width <int>
156:         height <int>
157:         background <#rrggbb>
158:         color <#rrggbb>               # text color (alias: colour)
159:         stroke <#rrggbb>              # border color
160:         strokeWidth <1-10>
161:         fontSize <int>
162:         border <solid|dashed|dotted>
163:         opacity <0-100>
164:         metadata <true|false>          # show/hide metadata line
165:         description <true|false>       # show/hide description
166:     }
167: }
168: ```
169: 
170: **Shapes**: `Box`, `RoundedBox`, `Circle`, `Ellipse`, `Hexagon`,
171: `Diamond`, `Cylinder`, `Pipe`, `Person`, `Robot`, `Folder`,
172: `WebBrowser`, `Window`, `Terminal`, `MobileDevicePortrait`,
173: `MobileDeviceLandscape`, `Component`

176: 
177: ```dsl
178: styles {
179:     relationship <tag> {
180:         thickness <int>
181:         color <#rrggbb>
182:         style <solid|dashed|dotted>
183:         routing <Direct|Orthogonal|Curved>
184:         fontSize <int>
185:         width <int>
186:         position <0-100>               # label position along line
187:         opacity <0-100>
188:     }
189: }
190: ```

193: 
194: Use the default tags:
195: 
196: ```dsl
197: styles {
198:     element "Element" { ... }           # applies to ALL elements
199:     relationship "Relationship" { ... } # applies to ALL relationships
200: }
201: ```
202:

204: 
205: ```dsl
206: styles {
207:     light {
208:         element "Person" { background #08427B; color #ffffff }
209:     }
210:     dark {
211:         element "Person" { background #1a6bc4; color #ffffff }
212:     }
213: }
214: ```
215:

217: 
218: ```dsl
219: styles {
220:     element "Person" {
221:         shape Person
222:         background #08427B
223:         color #ffffff
224:     }
225:     element "Software System" {
226:         background #1168BD
227:         color #ffffff
228:     }
229:     element "External" {
230:         background #999999
231:         color #ffffff
232:     }
233:     element "Container" {
234:         background #438DD5
235:         color #ffffff
236:     }
237:     element "Component" {
238:         background #85BBF0
239:         color #000000
240:     }
241:     element "Database" {
242:         shape Cylinder
243:     }
244:     element "Web" {
245:         shape WebBrowser
246:     }
247:     element "Queue" {
248:         shape Pipe
249:     }
250:     relationship "Relationship" {
251:         routing Orthogonal
252:     }
253:     relationship "Async" {
254:         style dashed
255:     }
256: }
257: ```
258: 
259: ## Themes
260: 
261: ```dsl
262: views {
263:     theme default                      # Structurizr default theme
264: }
265: ```
266: 
267: Built-in cloud themes (by name, no URL needed):
268: `amazon-web-services-2020.04.30`, `microsoft-azure-2021.01.26`,
269: `google-cloud-platform`, `kubernetes`. Custom styles override theme
270: defaults. Never reference a theme by URL — offline validation cannot
271: fetch it.
272: 
273: ## Terminology
274: 
275: Customize C4 terminology for your organization:
276: 
277: ```dsl
278: views {
279:     terminology {
280:         person "Actor"
281:         softwareSystem "Application"
282:         container "Service"
283:         component "Module"
284:         deploymentNode "Server"
285:         relationship "Dependency"
286:     }
287: }
288: ```
289: 
290: ## Configuration
291: 
292: ```dsl
293: configuration {
294:     scope <landscape|softwaresystem|none>
295:     visibility <private|public>
296:     users {
297:         "user@example.com" read
298:         "admin@example.com" write
299:     }
300: }
301: ```
302: 
303: ## Directives for existing elements
304: 
305: Modify elements or relationships defined elsewhere:
306: 
307: ```dsl
308: !element <identifier> {
309:     description "Updated description"
310:     tags "NewTag"
311: }
312: ```
313: 
314: Bulk operations:
315: 
316: ```dsl
317: !elements element.tag==Container {
318:     tags "Monitored"
319:     properties { "team" "platform" }
320: }
321: 
322: !relationships relationship.tag==Async {
323:     tags "EventDriven"
324: }
325: ```
326: 
327: ## Common patterns
328: 
329: ### Tagging for Filtered Views
330: 
331: ```dsl
332: model {
333:     system = softwareSystem "System" {
334:         api = container "API" "REST API" "Go" "Service,v2"
335:         legacyApi = container "Legacy API" "Old REST API" "Java" "Service,v1,Deprecated"
336:     }
337: }
338: views {
339:     container system "AllContainers" { include * }
340:     filtered "AllContainers" exclude "Deprecated" "CurrentContainers"
341: }
342: ```
343: 
344: ### Async/Sync Relationship Distinction
345: 
346: ```dsl
347: model {
348:     system.api -> system.db "queries" "SQL"
349:     system.api -> system.queue "publishes order events to" "AMQP" "Async"
350:     system.worker -> system.queue "consumes order events from" "AMQP" "Async"
351: }
352: views {
353:     styles {
354:         relationship "Async" { style dashed }
355:     }
356: }
357: ```

1: # DSL gotchas and errors
2: 
3: The failure modes of `workspace.dsl` text, the rule behind each one, and
4: how to write the DSL so it does not fail. The error strings are the
5: pinned Structurizr CLI's own output. Adapted from the Troubleshooting
6: table of the `structurizr-dsl` skill of `jrjsmrtn/c4-skills` (MIT, see
7: `NOTICE.md`) and the Structurizr documentation (`structurizr/
8: structurizr.github.io`, MIT); see `source-map.md` for the
9: passage-by-passage mapping.
10: 
11: ## Error table
12: 
13: | Error | Cause | Fix |
14: |---|---|---|
15: | `Too many tokens, expected: person <name> [description] [tags]` | An unquoted value with spaces, or more tokens than the statement still has | Quote the value (`"..."`), or skip the property with `""` |
16: | `The identifier "x" is already in use at line N` | Duplicate flat identifier (a second element reusing `x`) | Rename the second identifier — never delete the element |
17: | `The destination element "x" does not exist at line N` | Forward reference (the element is declared later) or a typo | Check the identifier first, then move the declaration above its first use. `The source element "x" does not exist` is the same error for the left side |
18: | `Unexpected token ... at line N` | `{` on its own line, or unbalanced braces | Move the `{` to the same line as the statement; close on a line of its own |
19: | `Relationships cannot be added between parents and children at line N` | A relationship from an element to its own child (system to its container) | Relate at the same level instead (person to container, container to container) |
20: | Implied relationship unwanted | Default behavior | Add `!impliedRelationships false` |
21: | View is empty | Elements not included | Add `include *` or specific `include` expressions |
22: | Duplicate relationship | Same source, destination and description | Give each relationship a unique description |
23: | `View keys can only contain the following characters: a-zA-Z0-9_-` | A view key with spaces or other characters | Use a plain camelCase key (`SystemContext`, `Containers`) — explicit keys only |
24: 
25: ## Declaration order
26: 
27: The DSL is parsed top to bottom: it is imperative, not declarative — the
28: model is built step by step in the order the lines appear (the DSL is a
29: wrapper over an imperative modeling library, and nothing is hoisted). An
30: element must be declared before any relationship that references it. A
31: forward reference fails with `The destination element "x" does not
32: exist at line N` — the same error as a typo, so check the identifier
33: first, then the order. Declare all elements first, then the
34: relationships.
35: 
36: Where a relationship must cross blocks (for example from an element
37: inside `a` to the element in scope inside `b`), the special `this`
38: keyword refers to the element in scope — write the relationship where
39: both ends are already declared, or use `this` on the near end.
40: 
41: ## Quoting
42: 
43: Quotes are optional only for a single token without spaces. Every name,
44: description, technology and metadata value that contains spaces must be
45: quoted; an unquoted phrase pushes its extra words into the following
46: positional properties, and once those are filled the parser fails with
47: `Too many tokens, expected: ...`. To leave an earlier optional property
48: empty while filling a later one, use `""` as its placeholder.
49: 
50: ## Relationship description and technology
51: 
52: Give every relationship both a description and a technology:
53: `a -> b "Reads orders from" "HTTPS/JSON"`.
54: 
55: - The description is a verb phrase from the source's point of view:
56:   "Reads orders from", "Publishes events to". Avoid "Uses" and "Calls".
57: - The technology answers "what would I edit or configure?":
58:   "Express Router", "Kafka topic orders.v1", "PostgreSQL 16" — not
59:   "JavaScript".
60: - A relationship without a technology (or without a description) still
61:   parses: `validate` answers cleanly, so this is authoring knowledge,
62:   not an error message — check it when you write or fix a relationship.
63: 
64: Between the same source and destination, the description is the
65: relationship's identity: two relationships with the same description are
66: a duplicate, and the only way to model two links between a pair is two
67: different descriptions.
68: 
69: ## Element descriptions
70: 
71: Give every element a description — people, systems, containers,
72: components and custom elements alike. A missing description also parses
73: cleanly (for a person or container it surfaces as an `inspect` finding,
74: for a custom element it does not surface at all), so it is authoring
75: knowledge, not an error message. For a custom `element`, the second
76: string is its **metadata** — that is where the human description goes.
77: 
78: ## Flat identifiers
79: 
80: Prefer flat identifiers. Skip `!identifiers hierarchical` unless two
81: elements would otherwise share an identifier — with hierarchical
82: identifiers every reference must spell out the full path
83: (`system.api`), and mistakes produce the same "element does not exist"
84: error as a typo. With flat identifiers, every identifier must be unique
85: across the whole workspace: a second `api` container in a second system
86: fails with `The identifier "api" is already in use`. When a fix means
87: renaming an identifier, rename every reference to it in the same pass.
88: 
89: ## Implied relationships
90: 
91: By default the DSL creates "implied relationships" automatically: a
92: relationship from a person to a container inside a software system
93: implies a relationship from the person to the software system (and
94: similarly for the other parent/child combinations). You never write the
95: implied relationship — it appears in the model and in views
96: automatically. `!impliedRelationships false` disables the creation;
97: there is also a strategy setting (`!impliedRelationships
98: com.structurizr.model.CreateImpliedRelationshipsUnlessSameRelationship
99: ExistsStrategy`) for finer control.
100: 
101: ## Explicit view keys
102: 
103: Give every view an explicit key: `systemContext bookshop "SystemContext"
104: { ... }`. The key may only contain `a-zA-Z0-9_-` — no spaces:
105: `"System Context"` fails with `View keys can only contain the following
106: characters: a-zA-Z0-9_-`. A view without a key gets an auto-generated
107: one that `inspect` flags, and that is not guaranteed to be stable over
108: time (you will likely lose manual layout information); a plain
109: camelCase key (`SystemContext`, `Containers`) avoids both.
110: 
111: ## Under the MCP
112: 
113: - The MCP works on the workspace's DSL text as a single input: no
114:   `!include`, no `!docs`, no `!adrs` — they are refused
115:   (`feature ... is not enabled`). Inline everything into the one file;
116:   that is expected under the MCP limits, not a defect to work around.
117: - The MCP cannot render images; its export tools emit PlantUML,
118:   C4-PlantUML or Mermaid **source** only.
119: - Never reference a theme by URL — offline validation cannot fetch it.
120: - Check the result with the MCP `validate` tool before you finish; a
121:   file that does not validate is not done.

5: pinned Structurizr CLI's own output. Adapted from the Troubleshooting
6: table of the `structurizr-dsl` skill of `jrjsmrtn/c4-skills` (MIT, see
7: `NOTICE.md`) and the Structurizr documentation (`structurizr/
8: structurizr.github.io`, MIT); see `source-map.md` for the
9: passage-by-passage mapping.
10: 
11: ## Error table
12: 
13: | Error | Cause | Fix |
14: |---|---|---|
15: | `Too many tokens, expected: person <name> [description] [tags]` | An unquoted value with spaces, or more tokens than the statement still has | Quote the value (`"..."`), or skip the property with `""` |
16: | `The identifier "x" is already in use at line N` | Duplicate flat identifier (a second element reusing `x`) | Rename the second identifier — never delete the element |
17: | `The destination element "x" does not exist at line N` | Forward reference (the element is declared later) or a typo | Check the identifier first, then move the declaration above its first use. `The source element "x" does not exist` is the same error for the left side |
18: | `Unexpected token ... at line N` | `{` on its own line, or unbalanced braces | Move the `{` to the same line as the statement; close on a line of its own |
19: | `Relationships cannot be added between parents and children at line N` | A relationship from an element to its own child (system to its container) | Relate at the same level instead (person to container, container to container) |
20: | Implied relationship unwanted | Default behavior | Add `!impliedRelationships false` |
21: | View is empty | Elements not included | Add `include *` or specific `include` expressions |
22: | Duplicate relationship | Same source, destination and description | Give each relationship a unique description |
23: | `View keys can only contain the following characters: a-zA-Z0-9_-` | A view key with spaces or other characters | Use a plain camelCase key (`SystemContext`, `Containers`) — explicit keys only |
24: 
25: ## Declaration order
26: 
27: The DSL is parsed top to bottom: it is imperative, not declarative — the
28: model is built step by step in the order the lines appear (the DSL is a
29: wrapper over an imperative modeling library, and nothing is hoisted). An
30: element must be declared before any relationship that references it. A
31: forward reference fails with `The destination element "x" does not
32: exist at line N` — the same error as a typo, so check the identifier
33: first, then the order. Declare all elements first, then the
34: relationships.
35: 
36: Where a relationship must cross blocks (for example from an element
37: inside `a` to the element in scope inside `b`), the special `this`
38: keyword refers to the element in scope — write the relationship where
39: both ends are already declared, or use `this` on the near end.
40: 
41: ## Quoting
42: 
43: Quotes are optional only for a single token without spaces. Every name,
44: description, technology and metadata value that contains spaces must be
45: quoted; an unquoted phrase pushes its extra words into the following
46: positional properties, and once those are filled the parser fails with
47: `Too many tokens, expected: ...`. To leave an earlier optional property
48: empty while filling a later one, use `""` as its placeholder.
49: 
50: ## Relationship description and technology
51: 
52: Give every relationship both a description and a technology:
53: `a -> b "Reads orders from" "HTTPS/JSON"`.
54: 
55: - The description is a verb phrase from the source's point of view:
56:   "Reads orders from", "Publishes events to". Avoid "Uses" and "Calls".
57: - The technology answers "what would I edit or configure?":
58:   "Express Router", "Kafka topic orders.v1", "PostgreSQL 16" — not
59:   "JavaScript".
60: - A relationship without a technology (or without a description) still
61:   parses: `validate` answers cleanly, so this is authoring knowledge,
62:   not an error message — check it when you write or fix a relationship.
63: 
64: Between the same source and destination, the description is the
65: relationship's identity: two relationships with the same description are
66: a duplicate, and the only way to model two links between a pair is two
67: different descriptions.
68: 
69: ## Element descriptions
70: 
71: Give every element a description — people, systems, containers,
72: components and custom elements alike. A missing description also parses
73: cleanly (for a person or container it surfaces as an `inspect` finding,
74: for a custom element it does not surface at all), so it is authoring
75: knowledge, not an error message. For a custom `element`, the second
76: string is its **metadata** — that is where the human description goes.
77: 
78: ## Flat identifiers
79: 
80: Prefer flat identifiers. Skip `!identifiers hierarchical` unless two
81: elements would otherwise share an identifier — with hierarchical
82: identifiers every reference must spell out the full path
83: (`system.api`), and mistakes produce the same "element does not exist"
84: error as a typo. With flat identifiers, every identifier must be unique
85: across the whole workspace: a second `api` container in a second system
86: fails with `The identifier "api" is already in use`. When a fix means
87: renaming an identifier, rename every reference to it in the same pass.
88: 
89: ## Implied relationships
90: 
91: By default the DSL creates "implied relationships" automatically: a
92: relationship from a person to a container inside a software system
93: implies a relationship from the person to the software system (and
94: similarly for the other parent/child combinations). You never write the
95: implied relationship — it appears in the model and in views
96: automatically. `!impliedRelationships false` disables the creation;
97: there is also a strategy setting (`!impliedRelationships
98: com.structurizr.model.CreateImpliedRelationshipsUnlessSameRelationship
99: ExistsStrategy`) for finer control.
100: 
101: ## Explicit view keys
102: 
103: Give every view an explicit key: `systemContext bookshop "SystemContext"
104: { ... }`. The key may only contain `a-zA-Z0-9_-` — no spaces:
105: `"System Context"` fails with `View keys can only contain the following
106: characters: a-zA-Z0-9_-`. A view without a key gets an auto-generated
107: one that `inspect` flags, and that is not guaranteed to be stable over
108: time (you will likely lose manual layout information); a plain
109: camelCase key (`SystemContext`, `Containers`) avoids both.
110: 
111: ## Under the MCP
112: 
113: - The MCP works on the workspace's DSL text as a single input: no
114:   `!include`, no `!docs`, no `!adrs` — they are refused
115:   (`feature ... is not enabled`). Inline everything into the one file;
116:   that is expected under the MCP limits, not a defect to work around.
117: - The MCP cannot render images; its export tools emit PlantUML,
118:   C4-PlantUML or Mermaid **source** only.
119: - Never reference a theme by URL — offline validation cannot fetch it.
120: - Check the result with the MCP `validate` tool before you finish; a
121:   file that does not validate is not done.
